nodes.title: POST /api/documents/:id/anchor answers status 'anchored' in its 202 body even when a mid-flight revoke kept the row revoked
nodes.description:
**BLUF:** after pull request 1814 (KS-1814), `POST /api/documents/:id/anchor` writes `status: 'anchored'` with `preserveTerminalStatuses: true`, so a revoke that lands while the anchoring call is in flight keeps `revoked` in the row. The handler still always answers `202` with `status: 'anchored'`; it never reads what `updateDocument` returned. The row is right; the response body misreports it. Found by QA gate 19 on pull request 1814 (finding 1814-2), measured over a mocked repository only.

**What was read and measured**

* The write: `updateDocument(id, tenantId, { blockchain, status: 'anchored' }, undefined, { preserveTerminalStatuses: true })` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1584-1587` at the pull request 1814 head `277e5ba6b7ae`; `:1534-1537` at develop `d7ddfa1f6433`, where the write has no options at all). documentRepo's KS-521 CASE keeps `revoked` / `deleted` when that option is set.
* The answer: `res.status(202).json({ id, status: 'anchored', transactionHash, blockchain })` (`:1611-1613` at the head; `:1560-1562` at develop). It does not read `updateDocument`'s return value, which is `Promise<DocumentRecord | null>` (`services/originate/src/repositories/documentRepo.ts`).
* Gate 19's cell B6: a mocked `updateDocument` that returns a revoked record. The body still says `anchored`.

**Fix shape (the gate's):** answer from the returned record, or say plainly that the row's status was not updated. Whether the real repository's returned record carries the kept `revoked` status was not measured, so read that before choosing.

**Priority 3:** the response is wrong but the stored data is right, so it is not a data-integrity defect. A caller that trusts the 202 body over a read-back would believe a revoked document is anchored.

**Not done:** no request against any box; no test written. The race window (a revoke during the anchoring call) was not driven against a database.
